question.problem:
Given that $\tan\theta = \dfrac{1}{4},$ find the value of $x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14244094/assets/f8affbac78c75000d7bbbc8c15508252f7bea0270fdf6cc9c5e5244eb89b505d.png)
question.worked_solution:
The tangent of an angle is equal to the opposite divided by the adjacent (T-O-A).

Relative to the angle $\theta,$ the length of the opposite side is $x-1,$ and the length of the adjacent side is $2x.$ Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡\theta  & =\frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}} \\ \frac{1}{4} & =\frac{x-1}{2x} \\ 2x & =4(x-1) \\ 2x & =4x-4 \\ 2x & =4 \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
